summary: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Welcker, Jahn, Schmidt, and Haupt. He held posts at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (professor, 1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1929).

Ulrike Roesler specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Münster and taught at Freiburg and Marburg. Later appointments include the University of Oxford (Professor, attested 2019) and Wolfson College (attested 2026).

Uma Chakravarti works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Miranda House, Mount Carmel College, University Law College, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She served as an educator at Miranda House (1966–1998).

Umakant Premanand Shah was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as deputy director (1954) and head of the Ramayana Project (1965) at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, and was director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1955–1975).

Umar Rolf von Ehrenfels was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1932–1937) and served as Head of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Madras (1949) and Guest-Professor at Heidelberg (1961).
Umberto Norsa was an Indology scholar who studied law at the University of Bologna from ~1884 to 1888. He served as secretary at the Gabinetto di Lettura di Mantova from 1893 to 1938.

Umesh Kumar Singh is an Indology scholar who completed his B.A. at the University of Allahabad (1997–2000), his M.A. at Banaras Hindu University (2000–2002), and his Ph.D. at the University of Delhi (2004–2010).

Umesha Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp. He worked at the University of Allahabad (~1923–1959), was founder secretary at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha (~1943–1967), and directed the Mithila Institute (~1951–1961).

Unapana Pemananda works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at South-Eastern Norway, Oslo, Peradeniya, and the University of Hong Kong (PhD 2022–2025). He held posts at the University of Oslo (2025) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology and related fields. He studied at Bharathiar University, Ayurveda College Coimbatore, Amsterdam, and Yokohama National University. His career includes posts at FRLHT (1995–2007), United Nations University (2010–2020), and The University of Trans-Disciplinary Health Sciences and Technology (2020).

Unrai Wogihara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University and the University of Strasbourg under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann. He served as a professor at Shukyo University (~1907–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1937).
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juze-kai (1884), Kairitsu Gakko, and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Unuwaturabubule Mahinda works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Oriental Studies Society, Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka, Sri Jayewardenepura (Ph.D.), and Kelaniya. His posts include University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2015–2018) and Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka (2026).

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and held an appointment as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Mongolian National University of Arts and Culture, Eötvös Loránd University, and UC Berkeley (PhD). Her posts include Herron School of Art and Design and Indiana University Bloomington (~2021).

Uranchimeg Tsultemin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, where she worked as a Lecturer in the Art History Department, and was an Associate Professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at Fribourg, Kyoto, and Temple University (Ph.D.) under DeMartino, Yanagida, Iriya, and Mair. He served as Associate Director at Hanazono University and the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (1989–1999).

Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist. She served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2001), where she is attested as Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia in 2026.

Usha R. Jain is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley. She served as Senior Lecturer Emerita at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2026) and as an RDH at Dr Ritu Punia DMD (2024).
Usharbudh Arya was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of London from ~1960 to 1967 and held a post at the University of Minnesota from ~1967 to 1973.
